item.title: Hong Kong gov’t mulls appeal after tycoon Jimmy Lai fraud conviction overturned
item.description: Hong Kong’s justice department will consider an appeal after a court overturned pro-democracy media tycoon Jimmy Lai’s fraud conviction relating to an alleged lease violation at the now-shuttered Apple Daily newspaper headquarters. His jail term stemming from the case was quashed on Thursday morning, though the 78-year-old media mogul still remains behind bars serving 20 years […]

item.title: Hong Kong gov’t to recruit journalism students to intern at mainland Chinese media outlets
item.description: The Hong Kong government is set to recruit journalism students to intern at mainland Chinese media outlets, as part of a new programme to promote the understanding of China’s development among local youth. The Home and Youth Affairs Bureau will roll out a new programme in July to provide Hong Kong journalism students with opportunities […]

item.title: Chief Exec. John Lee appoints SCMP publisher Tammy Tam to Law Reform Commission
item.description: South China Morning Post (SCMP) publisher Tammy Tam has been appointed by Chief Executive John Lee to the Law Reform Commission (LRC). item.title: Tai Po fire: Wang Fuk Court residents could return home for belongings as early as late April, official says
item.description: A senior Hong Kong official has said authorities will arrange for residents of the seven blocks gutted in November’s Wang Fuk Court fire to return home and gather personal belongings as early as late April. item.description: Hong Kong’s finance chief has defended the government’s plan to dip into a fund that ensures the stability of its currency peg to help finance a technology hub by the city’s border with mainland China, calling the move an “investment” rather than expenditure. item.title: ‘Deeply concerned’: China calls for Afghanistan-Pakistan ceasefire
item.description: China called on Friday for a ceasefire between Afghanistan and Pakistan, adding it was talking to both sides to try to end violent clashes that had left Beijing “deeply concerned”. item.title: Budget 2026: ‘Symphony of Lights’ to be retired in 2nd half of year, replaced by light shows at tourist spots
item.description: Hong Kong’s 22-year-old nightly “A Symphony of Lights” harbour display has “completed its historical mission” and will be replaced by holiday-themed light shows at multiple tourist attractions, authorities have said.
